title: Kymmenruudukko
instruction: Aseta nappuloita ruudukkoon — ja katso, paljonko tilaa on vielä jäljellä.
saidTidied: Nappuloita edelleen: {n}, ruutuja: {cap}. Vain järjestys muuttui.
gateBody: Kokoelma valmiita ruudukoita: sama luku viidellä tavalla aseteltuna, kymppikaverit, vertailtavia pareja sekä luvut yhdestätoista yhdeksääntoista kummassakin kahdenkymmenen ruudukossa. Ota rakentamasi ruudukot talteen ja palaa niihin myöhemmin.
_notes: PANEL: native linguist + 1.–2. luokan matematiikan opettaja + native B2C education-marketing writer. REBUILT, not translated. The fi strings already sitting in ten-frame.js:252-299 are a pre-panel HYPOTHESIS; we treated them as a draft to AUDIT, and we reject four of them outright (see DEFECTS).

⚠ THE SOURCE MOVED TWICE WHILE WE WORKED, so this file is written against the CURRENT artefact rather than against the brief. Round one (04:09): routinesBtn was DELETED from both _source-en.json and ten-frame.js; fieldTwentyField became 'Frame of twenty'; gateBody lost its print clause. Round two (later): trayAriaOne was ADDED. Net result is still 31 keys, but NOT the same 31 the brief described — routinesBtn is gone and trayAriaOne is new. We ship exactly the current source's key set, in its order. We did not ship routinesBtn: the tool no longer reads it, and a dead string is forbidden by the §23.6 A15 rule (the applier's ORDER check would refuse it in any case).

The lesson we are recording for the next panel: re-read the source at the END of the work, not only at the start. Our first validation pass compared against a source that had already changed, and reported 'extra key routinesBtn' — which looked like OUR error and was actually the artefact moving. Both times the check caught it only because it compared key SETS rather than trusting the count in the brief.
=== CASE TRAP 1 — trayAria. A REAL BUG IN THE SHIPPED DRAFT, FIXED MID-SESSION AT THE ARCHITECTURE LEVEL. ===

The draft read 'Alusta — {n} nappulaa jäljellä'. In Finnish a numeral GOVERNS its noun: >1 takes the partitive singular ('3 nappulaa') but 1 takes the NOMINATIVE singular ('1 nappula'). left = cap − count, so left = 1 is reachable in all five fields and the string would have rendered the ungrammatical '1 nappulaa jäljellä'. A bare .replace cannot express that alternation, so our first answer restructured the sentence to be immune: the head noun carried the case ('nappuloita', partitive plural governed by the existential 'jäljellä') and the colon demoted {n} to a read-out value.

⚠ THAT IS NO LONGER THE ANSWER WE SHIP, BECAUSE THE TOOL CHANGED UNDER US. A dedicated singular key trayAriaOne was added mid-session and ten-frame.js:1050-1052 now branches left<=0 → trayEmptyAria, left===1 → trayAriaOne, else → trayAria. We VERIFIED that branch in the current file before relying on it. With the singular split out, trayAria is only ever reached at n >= 2, so the idiomatic quantifier form is now both safe and better Finnish, and we take it: 'Rasia — {n} nappulaa jäljellä' (partitive singular, correct for every n >= 2) alongside 'Rasia — yksi nappula jäljellä' (nominative singular after 'yksi'). The colon workaround was correct engineering for the old shape; the new shape deserves the natural sentence.

DEFECT F (CODE/CONTENT, fr + it + es — found by measuring, not by reading) — the new trayAriaOne names the TRAY differently from trayAria and trayEmptyAria in three locales: fr 'La barquette' vs 'Le plateau', it 'La vaschetta' vs 'Il vassoio', es 'La reserva' vs 'La bandeja'. The tray is ONE of the tool's three named parts (ten-frame.js:15-16), so a screen-reader user in those three languages hears it called two different things depending on how many counters are in it. en/de/pt/nl/sv/da/no/fi are consistent. Ours is 'Rasia' in all three keys, deliberately.
=== CASE TRAP 2 — saidField, the {field} token. ===

{field} is filled at ten-frame.js:1048 with a field NAME in the nominative (_fieldName → api.t(labelKey)). Any Finnish sentence embedding it would demand a case ('Viiden ruudukossa…' inessive, 'Viiden ruudukkoon…' illative), and a fixed nominative token cannot supply one. The precedent is recorded in this repo at part-whole-frame.js:449-451 — label+number concatenation broke Finnish case-marking on open-number-line, caught by three ensembles.

SOLUTION — we did NOT embed it. {field} is left as a STANDALONE NAMING UTTERANCE closed by a full stop, and the information that followed it in EN is carried by a second, self-contained clause with its own head nouns: '{field}. Nappuloita: {n}, ruutuja: {cap}.' Nominative is the correct and only form for a naming utterance, so the token is grammatical by construction and needs no inflection. Same manoeuvre a sibling used for markerAria.
=== CASE TRAP 3 — filledAt, and why we KEPT the draft's shape. ===

{n} here is NOT a count — ten-frame.js:1016 fills it with the CELL ORDINAL (i+1), and the sibling branch at :1017 emits the bare ordinal for an empty cell. The design (comment at :1010-1014) requires the ordinal to LEAD so the run-length is audible on a serial read.

'{n}, nappula' is therefore correct and we keep it: the comma makes this an APPOSITION ('7, a counter'), not a quantifier phrase, so the noun is NOT governed by the numeral and stays NOMINATIVE SINGULAR. Written '{n} nappula' without the comma, a Finn parses it as a broken quantifier phrase wanting '7 nappulaa'. THE COMMA IS LOAD-BEARING — it must not be tidied away by a later cleanup.
=== CASE TRAP 4 — saidBoard / saidRoom / saidFull, the 'n of cap' idiom. ===

Spoken Finnish for '3 of 10' is 'kolme kymmenestä' — the ELATIVE falls on cap, which is a fixed token. Every construction that reads naturally ('{n} nappulaa {cap} ruudussa') needs BOTH numbers to govern inflection ('kymmenessä ruudussa'), so a digit token makes them all ungrammatical. The draft dodged this with a slash ('{n} / {cap}') — see DEFECT E.

SOLUTION — one label:value readout reused across all five announcements, nouns carrying the case, numbers as free values: 'Nappuloita: {n}, ruutuja: {cap}.' Grammatical at n = 0 and n = 1 (where 'Nappuloita 3' WITHOUT the colon would not be), honest, and strictly MORE informative than the EN because it names what the {cap} counts — ruudut. A screen-reader user learns one pattern and then hears it everywhere.

saidRoom's second clause avoids the same trap with a numeral SUBJECT, which takes a 3sg verb and no inflected noun: 'Vielä {left} mahtuu.' Correct at left = 1 ('yksi mahtuu') and left = 7 ('seitsemän mahtuu').

saidTidied's whole job is the invariant, so we STATE it rather than imply it: 'Nappuloita edelleen: {n}, ruutuja: {cap}. Vain järjestys muuttui.' — still N counters, only the ARRANGEMENT changed. A screen-reader user has no other way to learn that Tidy did not change the number.
=== DEFECTS — the English and the code, not only our own copy. ===
DEFECT A (fi draft, ten-frame.js:284) — the numeral-agreement bug above. Would have shipped '1 nappulaa'. Fixed here by restructure.

DEFECT B (fi draft, ten-frame.js:284-285) — 'Alusta' for the tray is a HOMOGRAPH of the commonest reset idiom in this product. As an adverb 'alusta' means 'from the beginning', and 'Aloita alusta' ships in SIXTEEN tool files including part-whole-frame.js, which also ships nappula — the same tool family teaches the reader the other sense. 'Alusta — tyhjä' reads as 'Start over — empty'. Rejected. No English-side check could have seen this.

DEFECT C (ENGLISH SOURCE) — RAISED BY US, AND ALREADY CORRECTED MID-SESSION. The source read 'Field of twenty', a calque of the German Zwanzigerfeld, which minted a FOURTH named noun ('field') against the tool's own header law at ten-frame.js:15-16: 'THE FRAME · THE COUNTER · THE TRAY. Three named parts, and nothing else in this tool gets a noun.' An English teacher says 'twenty frame' or 'double ten frame'. It is now 'Frame of twenty' — correct. Finnish had already declined the calque ('kenttä' is not the Finnish term for this apparatus), so fi needs no change and ships three nouns as the header requires.

DEFECT C-RESIDUAL (ENGLISH, STILL OPEN) — gateBody still says 'the teens on both FIELDS' after the chip was renamed to 'Frame of twenty'. One noun left behind by the rename; it should read 'on both frames' (or name them: 'on the frame of twenty and the two frames of ten'). Our fi says 'kummassakin kahdenkymmenen ruudukossa' and is unaffected.

DEFECT D — RETRACTED, VERIFIED FIXED. We found keepsBtn serving three roles (drawer text, the ADD button's aria-label, every saved item's aria-label) — the '#42 one element wearing two jobs under one aria-label' class. Re-reading the CURRENT file before reporting: it is fixed. The '+' now carries no duplicate name (with a comment at :1298-1299 naming the defect) and saved items use _fieldName(k.g), a genuinely distinct and informative name. We record it only to confirm the fix landed — reporting it as live would have been the 'verify the measurement before reporting the defect' trap.

DEFECT E (fi draft, ten-frame.js:291-295) — the slash in '{n} / {cap}'. A screen reader voices it as a word and a 7-year-old reads it as a fraction, in a tool whose REFUSES #10 forbids an equation on the stage. Replaced by the label:value readout.

MINOR (current code, :1295-1297) — the '+' add button's only accessible name is its '+' textContent. Inside a group named 'Talteen' that is understandable, so we are not calling it a defect, but a short authored name would read better than 'plus, button'. Flagged, not fixed — it would need a new key.
=== SIBLING COLLISIONS — every noun checked against the shipped FINNISH lexicon, not against English. ===

TRAY — 'lokero' is TAKEN: it is money-mat's tray in Finnish (money-core.js:55, 'lokerosi – napauta kolikkoa ottaaksesi sen pois'). 'tarjotin' is TAKEN: fraction-kitchen ships 'Täytä tarjotin' and 'Tarjotinpiste'. 'astia' is TAKEN: fraction-kitchen / measurement-bench ('Valitse astia', 'korkeaan astiaan'). 'alusta' rejected per DEFECT B. RULING: 'Rasia' — free as a part-name (the only hits anywhere are the incidental compound 'eväsrasia' in reading-easel and story-line CONTENT prose), and it is precisely the shallow tub a Finnish classroom keeps nappulat in.

We also rejected 'kippo', which is completely free and warmer: things PILE in a bowl, and the tray's whole job is that its contents can be counted at a glance. The pedagogy chose the noun over the warmth.

COUNTER — 'nappula' is the confirmed house word, already shipped by part-whole-frame.js ('Siirrä yksi nappula') and sound-boxes.js. Like EN 'counter' it is shared MATERIAL vocabulary, not an exclusive part-name, so consistency is right and we keep it.

GRID — 'ruudukko' is generic Finnish for a cell-grid and the stem of the locked title. wodb.js:49-50 uses it for its own 2×2 puzzle ('Viikon ruudukko', 'Omat ruudukot'), which is why keepsBtn is NOT 'Omat ruudukot' — that string is verbatim WODB's. frameAria stays the bare 'Ruudukko' rather than 'Kymmenruudukko', because the frame is a five, a ten or a twenty depending on the field and naming it after ten would be FALSE in three of the five.

'ruutu' (cell) is sanctioned by the header's own census (ten-frame.js:22, 'frame, cell, counter and tray were free') and already lives inside the locked title, so using it in the announcements mints nothing new.
'hyppy' confirmed unavailable — number-line owns it ('Kumoa viimeinen hyppy', 'Hyppyjä: {n}'), and its rabbit uses 'loikka' besides. Not needed here.
gateCta 'Katso Opettaja-tilaus' matches the shipped plan name verbatim (part-whole-frame.js), and 'kuuluu Opettaja-tilaukseen' is the house gate register. Contains 'Opettaja' as required.
=== THE THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS PUT TO US ===

1. 'kymppikaverit' — YES, right register. It is what Finnish 1.–2. luokka teachers and the standard textbook series call the complements to ten, and it is a single lexical unit exactly as the shipped sv 'tiokamraterna' / da 'tiervennerne' / no 'tiervennene' are. We prefer the compound over the draft's looser genitive phrase 'kympin kaverit': the compound is the NAME of the thing, the phrase only describes it, and a teacher scanning a paid-gate blurb is looking for the name.

2. The counters — 'nappulat', confirmed by classroom usage AND by the shipped sibling lexicon. Rejected 'laskupalikat' (palikka is a BLOCK/cube — wrong object, and place-value-lab already uses palikka for its unit cubes), 'pelimerkit' (gambling chips), 'napit' (buttons, too literal).

3. The verb for making a scattered set line up — 'Järjestä'. Rejected 'Siisti' (tidy as in clean up — implies the scatter was a MESS the child made wrongly, a soft verdict, and REFUSES #1-2 forbid verdicts), 'Suorista' (straighten — implies crookedness, not arrangement), 'Kokoa' (gather — implies collecting them up OFF the frame, the opposite of what the control does). 'Järjestä' is 'put in order': it names the arrangement and says nothing about the child.
=== A RULING THE FILE EXPLICITLY ASKS THE PANEL FOR ===

GEOMETRY_BY_LOCALE (ten-frame.js:221-234) ships every locale on 'default' until its native ensemble rules, and records that a renderer-true per-locale claim is a fact about a school system. FINNISH RULING: KEEP THE DEFAULT — single 'ten', twenty 'twentypair'. Finnish primary materials build twenty as TWO ten-frames (kaksi kymmenruudukkoa); the one-block Zwanzigerfeld with a five-break is a German convention and is not what a Finnish 1. luokka child meets first. The twentyfield chip should stay available — it is a good thing to be able to show — but it is not Finland's default. No code change requested: this ruling CONFIRMS the shipped default rather than altering it.
=== SMALLER CALLS ===

counterLabel 'Nappulat' — this key labels the COLOUR swatch row (ten-frame.js:312, settings key 'color'). Other tools' Finnish names the property ('Nappuloiden väri'). We kept the bare material name to match the EN's deliberate 'Counters', because four visible swatches make the property self-evident. Flagged so the operator can overrule.
fieldTen is 'Kymmenruudukko', identical to the tool title. Deliberate, and it has precedent — de ships Zehnerfeld for both. The ten-frame IS this tool's own field.

fieldFive is the transparent genitive phrase 'Viiden ruudukko', not a coined compound 'Viisiruudukko': 'kymmenruudukko' is a LEXICALISED Finnish term and 'viisiruudukko' is not, so coining it to force symmetry would read as invented. Finnish tolerates exactly this asymmetry between an established compound and a descriptive phrase.

The two twenties contrast on structure, not on a borrowed noun: 'Kahdenkymmenen ruudukko' (one frame holding twenty) vs 'Kaksi kymmenruudukkoa' (two frames of ten). Unmistakable apart, and neither needs 'kenttä'.

gateBody follows the CURRENT EN scope: the print clause is gone, and the closing line is 'Ota rakentamasi ruudukot talteen ja palaa niihin myöhemmin' — which also echoes the keepsBtn label 'Talteen', so the gate names the feature the button opens. Numbers spelled out ('yhdestätoista yhdeksääntoista') to match the shipped sv/da/no gate bodies.

No verdict or score word appears anywhere ('Täynnä' is a state of the apparatus, not a judgement of a child). No string asks a question that has an answer. No invisible characters; the only non-ASCII are Finnish letters and the em-dash the siblings already use.
